open_errors.issue: Asha's four are pursuing from behind, up from the waystone side. Later in the chapter they 'have reached the foot of the Saddle' and are 'climbing the slope', and they watch 'the ridge behind them'. But Meera first spots them on 'the first folds of the south slope', which is the far side where the crew ledge and Rope-Hut lie, ahead of her.
open_errors.fix: Place the first sighting back down the climb behind them.

patches.find: She looked down the long scoured fall of the Saddle to where it broke into the first folds of the south slope, and there, a very long way below, something moved that was not the wind.
patches.replace: She looked back down the long scoured fall of the Saddle to where it broke into the climb from the waystone, and there, a very long way below, something moved that was not the wind.

open_errors.issue: Rohan's Salt Fox question is called 'the same question as three nights ago'. He actually asked it on the first night of the rope (ch 4). Three nights earlier (ch 10) the question was Meera's, about his coat.
open_errors.fix: Point the callback at the first night of the rope.

patches.find: It was the same question as three nights ago. He knew that, and so did she.
patches.replace: It was the same question he had put to her on the first night of the rope. He knew that, and so did she.

open_errors.issue: Kiran's fever breaks the dawn after Sunni's burial (day 14). If he then sleeps 'two days and half a night', chapter 21 falls on day 16. The book's later chain fixes the Fair five days after chapter 21, which is also the 'fifteen days' of rope in ch 23 and the 'sixteen days' in ch 26. That chain lands the Fair on day 21. Chapter 29 calls it 'the dawn of day twenty', matching the twenty-day deadline.
open_errors.fix: Shorten Kiran's sleep by a day.

patches.find: He had slept two days and half a night, and Nimmi had stood over him with a lamp and pronounced the fever broken, and then said it again, as if she did not trust it.
patches.replace: He had slept a day and half a night, and Nimmi had stood over him with a lamp and pronounced the fever broken, and then said it again, as if she did not trust it.

open_errors.issue: Kiran says he has 'never known' what Dilan's last words 'sorry about the hymn' meant. But in ch 29 he says Dilan sang the hymn all the way down the line and he told him to shut up. Rohan had also told him about the hymn in ch 21.
open_errors.fix: Let Kiran know what the apology referred to.

patches.find: "He said *sorry about the hymn.* I don't know what that means. I've never known what it means."
patches.replace: "He said *sorry about the hymn.* He'd sung it the whole way down, and I'd told him to shut up. That was what he chose to be sorry for."

open_errors.issue: Kiran says Dilan bound them knot to wrist ('Knot on my wrist, knot on his'), but then that Dilan cut the rope 'above his waist'. Rohan's piece is a forearm's length ending in Dilan's whipped end, which fits a cut near the wrist.
open_errors.fix: Move the cut to just above Dilan's wrist.

patches.find: Then he had his knife. He cut his own rope above his waist, and it went slack, and I stopped.
patches.replace: Then he had his knife. He cut his own rope a forearm above his wrist, and it went slack, and I stopped.

open_errors.issue: Varun was assigned as Meera's rope partner in ch 2 and walked behind her up the gully in ch 3, so he knows her face as Jassi's second. In ch 25 he asks 'Who is the woman?' and the narration says 'He did not know her'. He should not know she is the Salt Fox, but he should recognise her.
open_errors.fix: Varun recognises her as the Kothi guide but not as the Salt Fox.

patches.replace: "And the woman?" said Varun. "Jassi's second, from Kothi. I'd have sworn the gully kept her."
"It did not. She came out of it with me."

patches.find: He was looking at a woman in a stained pattu with a hole in the hem. He did not know her, and Rohan understood in that moment how thin the single thread of her safety was, and that it ran through him.
patches.replace: He was looking at a woman in a stained pattu with a hole in the hem, the goat-man's second he had once walked behind up a gully. He did not know what else she was, and Rohan understood in that moment how thin the single thread of her safety was, and that it ran through him.

open_errors.issue: Varun crossed the Saddle bound at the Shilak Cairn to a salt-road man (ch 24). Yet he says of the jogini binding 'I'd heard of it, never seen one' and asks whether it holds.
open_errors.fix: Varun speaks from his own crossing.

patches.find: "A jogini binding! On the Shilak! I'd heard of it, never seen one."
patches.replace: "A jogini binding! I tied one myself to get here, to a salt-road man who smelled of fish. I never thought to see you in one."

patches.find: "And it holds? She can't leave you?"
patches.replace: "It holds you as it held me, then. She can't leave you."

open_errors.issue: Meera tells her bound partner 'I'm well' while believing she is dying of cold, and says it to be believed. Nothing happens, and the narration says the mountain 'had no jurisdiction over well'. The bible defines a lie as a statement believed false and said to be believed. It also says the rule is never suspended in a crisis.
open_errors.fix: Make her answer a true evasion instead of a free lie.

patches.find: It was true by the measure of the rope, though she was a long way from well, and she supposed it was true in the narrow sense that she was breathing. The mountain had no jurisdiction over *well*.
patches.replace: It was true by the measure of the rope. She was a long way from well, and she had not said she was. She had said only that she was breathing.

open_errors.issue: In ch 1 Meera stitches the brass button into the count's spine just before this crossing. In ch 28 the binding stitches hiding it are said to have been sewn 'ten winters back'.
open_errors.fix: Date the stitches to this crossing.

patches.find: She had sewn them herself, ten winters back, so that nobody would find what lay under them unless he meant to take the book apart.
patches.replace: She had sewn them herself the morning before the crossing, so that nobody would find what lay under them unless he meant to take the book apart.

open_errors.issue: Rohan's bound promise in ch 27 is 'I won't ask you anything else about that rope'. Ch 28 restates it as a promise of 'no more questions' at all. On that reading his later questions to Meera would break a bound promise and strike him as a great lie: 'May I?' in ch 29, 'What are you counting?' in ch 30, 'Count what?' in ch 31.
open_errors.fix: Restate the promise with its real scope and keep his caution.

patches.find: He had promised her no more questions, and he meant to keep the promise down to its smallest corner.
patches.replace: He had promised her no more questions about that rope, and he did not yet trust himself to know where its edges lay.
